title

three more ways to model a transaminase

the same reaction, from three other points of view

alanine transaminase · modelled as a medium, as a quantum, and as a partition depth

kundai sachikonye · extending the demo model, not replacing it

The demo deck already names the gaps

TransaminationReaction is a defined class over participants and roles. HermiT derives three reactions; the control drops out.

The demo deck ends by naming what that signature cannot constrain — mechanism, mass balance, PLP dependence. Each would need a different kind of model.

not carried by the OWL modelwhat it would take
which way the reaction runsa medium — a model of scarcity
when two readings are the samea derived quantum, not three tuned thresholds
how fast, and why that fasta partition depth over categorical layers

The first is not an omission. A reaction identifier is direction-symmetric by construction — the graph cannot hold direction even in principle.

Modelling the solution the reaction sits in

Represent the medium as a reservoir: an abundance for every species, and a weight for what it costs to individuate one out of it.

the mediumabundance per species
→
the weightscarce = cheap to pick out
→
the bias Δproducts − reactants
$ how the bias is computed
Δ = 0
for x in products:    Δ += w(abundance[x])
for x in reactants:   Δ -= w(abundance[x])
return Δ

# reverse the chain -> products and reactants swap
# -> every term changes sign -> Δ flips. by construction.

Only two properties of w are load-bearing: monotone in scarcity, bounded below by β. §7 re-runs every structural result under four unrelated weight families to check nothing depends on the logarithm.

Three cases, and the third one is a refusal

Compare the bias against the floor β. Exactly one of three holds — a trichotomy, not a threshold to tune.

reverseΔ < −β
undirected|Δ| ≤ β
forwardΔ > β
−β
+β

The middle band is the one that matters: the model declines rather than guessing. Both refusals are proved attainable by objects the language can construct — a refusal that never fires is not a refusal.

So reversibility is a property of the pair (reaction, medium) — never of the reaction alone.

Neither enzyme differs in the reaction it performs. Both curators are correct. Different media, opposite sign of Δ — a corollary rather than a curation decision.

Modelling when two readings count as the same

Any monitor is a finite process — finite states, finite bandwidth, finite time.

finite observeran axiom, not today's hardware
→
β > 0no reading returns a point
→
τ = βthe smallest distinction

Every identification carries irreducible residual uncertainty — not from noise, from the observer being finite. A model that separates two states closer than β would need a monitor the first box rules out.

So set the quantum τ = β: the tightest granularity consistent with what can be observed at all. Derived, not configured.

A validation check asserts β > 0 rather than assuming it — a floor of zero collapses everything downstream, so it gets a test of its own.

Why an ontology needs this

A working ontology is three things at once, each with its own idea of when two things are the same entity.

its identity question
the vocabularywhen are two classes the same class?
the instance storewhen are two records the same entity?
the consumerswhen is a returned match close enough to act on?
(i) vocabulary
⇒
(ii) store
⇑            ⇓
(iii) consumers
a cycle, so all three are equivalent
checked by exhaustive enumeration over every assignment of a small instance:
3
in the closed set
1
in the clearing set
so closure is strictly weaker than clearing — the equivalence does work rather than restating itself

Keeping three thresholds consistent is normally an engineering problem — tuned, drifting, never quite done. Here they are one number in three roles.

Modelling how fast, and why that fast

Bounded phase space ⟹ finitely many distinguishable states, and a rate floor ν_floor = 10¹⁰ s⁻¹.

k    = ν_floor · exp(−ΔM)
ΔM   = Σ log_b(kᵢ)

log₁₀(k_cat/K_M) ≈ 10 − d_C
# no fitted parameters

Diffusion-limited enzymes are the d_C = 1 case — which is why they cluster where they do.

counting d_C for a transaminase
1bulk solution → amino acid
↓
2amino acid → L-α-amino acid
↓
3→ the PLP-bound pose
dC = 3  →  log₁₀(kcat/KM) ≈ 7

d_C counts categorical layers — classes, not molecules. That is the same level the OWL definition already works at, so the law reads off the participant-role structure the defined class already carries.

And one of them runs against your endpoints today

The demo federates ChEBI → Rhea → UniProt. On a finite query budget, how should a client spend it across those joins?

The standard answer is water-filling — equalise marginal yield. It assumes diminishing returns. But a join needs both sides drawn, so yield goes as the square of a saturating coverage — and squaring a saturating function gives a sigmoid.

Water-filling assumes the whole curve is concave. Below the inflection it is convex, so the premise fails and the recipe inverts.

$ the gate, in full
N = COUNT(joinable keys)

if budget < N / 4:
    return concentrate
else:
    return water_fill
97%worst loss from spreading below the gate
0budgets below N/4 where spreading won

No fitted constant — N/4 falls out of the algebra for every corpus size. The ordering reverses above the threshold, so the gate changes the answer in both directions.

Where each model is thin

Stated once, because each is the kind of thing a reader finds anyway.

what it still needs
the mediumthe first direction sweep was one-sided — flooding a product cannot reverse a reaction, only depleting a reactant can. A real property of the model I did not anticipate.
pylonthe utilisation theorem first stated a slot's contribution as a ratio, which gave a boundary solution. Fixed by a different functional form, not a different constant.
partition depththe 140 suites largely check internal consistency. I audited them and found thirteen checks structurally incapable of failing.

All three are recorded where they happened rather than in a footnote here — the first two in the theorems' own text.

Why I am bringing three points of view rather than one

The questions an ontology cannot answer need different kinds of model — not a bigger OWL file.

The gate runs today — no hardware, just a COUNT against endpoints you already query.

The depth model predicts a temperature series — tedious, standard, and exactly what automated screening makes cheap.

Four models of one reaction, developed separately, that turned out to share a construction. I would rather bring three points of view and argue about them than one and defend it.
